items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 23, 2026
items.excerpt: - Libya’s eastern-based government files UN complaint over Benghazi ship attacks Libya’s eastern-based government said late Sunday that it filed a formal complaint with the UN General Assembly and Security Council seeking an international investigation into attacks on Russian and Maltese ships off the coast of Benghazi. Osama Hammad, head of Libya’s parliament-appointed government, said the investigation should establish whether Ukrainian personnel or military facilities were present in Libya and whether sites in the west had been used to prepare and launch explosive-laden drone boats. “We call on Ukraine to provide an official explanation of its military activities in Libya,” Hammad said. He also called for the drones’ operators and logistical backers to be identified and held accountable, regardless of nationality or position, and said Libyan territory, ports and facilities must not be used in foreign conflicts. Earlier Sunday, the government said preliminary findings indicated that a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base had likely been hit by drones following a pre-dawn explosion. Libyan broadcasters later reported a separate drone boat attack on a commercial vessel off the coast near the port. There was no immediate comment from Russia or Ukraine. - COP31 president closes climate summit without deal, blames some countries for failed talks COP31 President Murat Kurum formally closed the UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye without an agreement, criticizing some countries for failing to show the flexibility and commitment needed to reach a consensus. ... - Democrats secure largest US House majority since 1992 with 258 seats Democrats have secured 258 seats in the US House of Representatives following the Nov. 3 midterm elections, marking their strongest performance in the chamber in over three decades, according to election results reported by the Associated Press. The party reached the milestone after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated longtime Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District following a recount. Hubbard led Foxx by 330 votes out of approximately 287,000 cast, according to AP. The victory brought Democrats' total gains to 44 seats nationwide, surpassing the 40 seats the party gained in the 2018 midterm elections during President Donald Trump's first term.

items.title: Weekly Market Recap | J.P. Morgan Asset Management
items.excerpt: 23/11/2026 ... Thought of the week U.S. inflation remains elevated, with price pressures extending beyond energy into a wider range of goods and services. Core CPI rose 0.3% for the third consecutive month in Oct, highlighting the persistence of underlying inflation. Shelter remained the largest contributor, while transportation, recreation and medical care services also added to price pressures. Meanwhile, higher energy and import costs, alongside the delayed effects of earlier tariffs, are gradually filtering through to consumer prices as businesses seek to recover rising operating expenses. Although moderating wage growth may provide some relief, the lagged impact of earlier cost increases could keep inflation elevated even as the initial energy shock fades. Looking ahead, broadening price pressures across goods and services may complicate the Federal Reserve’s path towards its 2% inflation target.

items.title: Economic Week Ahead: Inflation, GDP and Jobs Data Follow Wall Street Selloff | Investing.com
items.excerpt: ## (1) PCED October’s core PCED (Wed) follows September’s 0.3% m/m gain. The Cleveland Fed’s Inflation Nowcasting tracking model projects another 0.3% m/m for both core and headline PCED. That would lift the y/y rates to 3.2% and 3.8% from September’s 3.1% and 3.6%. The core PPI final demand for personal consumption rose 4.8% y/y in October, well above the core CPI’s 2.6% (chart). PCED computers and peripheral equipment rose 9.7% y/y in September, up from August’s 8.4%. PPI electronic components rose faster, to 31.8% in October from September’s 26.8%, widening the gap (chart). That points to a continuation of elevated inflation in tech goods in the coming months. ## (2) GDP The second estimate of Q3 GDP (Wed) follows the advance estimate of 3.4% saar, with the GDP price index up 2.3%. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimates Q4 growth at 3.2% as of November 18, led by a 12.2% jump in business equipment spending (chart). A modest cyclical slowdown is possible through mid-2027. Growth has rested on a robust consumer, strong business spending, and a federal deficit near 6% of GDP during an expansion. Both consumer spending and business investment are likely to slow, with data center activity at risk after the midterms. Earnings growth should slow in tandem. The slowdown should be modest. It means the Fed won’t need to move far into restrictive territory, but it still needs to get back to neutral with a 50bps increase in the federal funds rate, in our opinion.

items.title: Speaker Johnson struggles with member attendance during final sessions
items.excerpt: House Republicans have just three weeks left in session to advance their legislative priorities before Democrats take control of Congress in January, leaving a narrow window to push through an assortment of unfinished business. At the top of the list is reaching an agreement on a stopgap measure, known as a continuing resolution (CR), or passing all 12 appropriations bills before the Dec. 11 funding deadline to avert a government shutdown. Republicans also face pressure to get the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), permitting reform legislation, a farm bill and other items across the finish line. But it won’t be an easy task for Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) to wrangle his caucus, especially as he struggles to keep his own members in Washington long enough to get the work done. Attendance problems have already begun disrupting the House floor schedule. GOP leaders postponed a procedural rule vote Wednesday over absences and canceled Friday’s votes altogether. Twenty-one Republicans missed votes on Thursday morning, following 14 absences the previous day. Johnson will need near-unanimous support on any procedural rule if he decides to bring a bill to the floor via regular order, requiring most of his conference to be present as he juggles a razor-thin margin. The House this week took up bills under a fast-track process known as suspension of the rules, which requires a two-thirds majority for passage and is typically reserved for legislation with broad bipartisan support. Because those bills often attract significant Democratic backing, Republicans can afford absences without jeopardizing passage.

items.title: AP Entertainment SummaryBrief at 7:01 a.m. EST | Features | rutlandherald.com
items.excerpt: Miley Cyrus marries rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate Palm Springs wedding Singer Miley Cyrus has married rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate ceremony in Palm Springs, California. Cyrus shared news of Saturday's wedding on Instagram, showing photos of the couple embracing in front of a white backdrop with a palm tree. Cyrus wore a long-sleeve silk Saint Laurent gown, while Morando sported a single-breasted tuxedo and dark sunglasses. The pair have been together since 2021, when they met on a blind date. Morando plays for the band Liily. Audience evacuated from Don Toliver concert after unknown substance released in the crowd LONDON (AP) — British police have evacuated over 12,000 fans from a Don Tolliver concert after an unknown substance was released in the crowd. Greater Manchester Police received reports Sunday night of people affected by what was initially believed to be tear gas at the Co-op Live arena. Social media footage showed concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths. Authorities declared a "major incident" to coordinate emergency services. One person was hospitalized, and more than 50 were assessed for eye and respiratory symptoms. Police are investigating the substance and how the incident occurred. ... Amy Poehler returns to TV with 'Dig' — just in time for Thanksgiving Amy Poehler returns to TV comedy for the first time in over 10 years with new show, “Dig” which is set on an archaeological excavation in Greece. It's been 11 years since “Parks and Recreation” and the new show reunites her with co-creator Mike Schur. Poehler says she'd always thought being an archaeologist was a fake job but researching her role as dig leader Elise got her fascinated with the stories uncovered in the dirt. “Dig” also stars Hugh Laurie, Antonia Thomas, Geraldine Viswanathan and Fina Strazza. Poehler says she loved the time she spent in Greece for the show, especially the people, food and history. A resurgent ‘Hunger Games’ goes big at the box office, despite competition of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' NEW YORK (AP) — “The Hunger Games” movie franchise rediscovered its box-office might, as “Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted with an estimated $120 million in North American theaters over the weekend. The sun had seemed to be setting on “The Hunger Games” as a cultural force. The previous chapter, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” grossed about half as much as the Jennifer Lawrence-led films. But “Sunrise on the Reaping” launched with $225 million globally, and it did it while a significant portion of potential moviegoers were locked at home playing “Grand Theft Auto VI.” Amazon MGM Studios’ “I Play Rocky” came in second with $9.3 million. Peter Farrelly's comic drama about the making of “Rocky” scored a rare “A+” CinemaScore. ... Associated Press critic Mark Kennedy says the soundtrack kicks off with an unexpected yacht rock ... Highlights include “Flower in a Hurricane” by Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, and “Power Trip” by K-pop star Jennie.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 23 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Kartik Aaryan launches Dopamine Studios with Kaaliya On his 35th birthday, Kartik Aaryan launched Dopamine Studios and announced monster thriller Kaaliya as its first film. ABP Live reports it is a Dharma Productions collaboration directed by Sandeep Modi, and the first-look poster went out on 22 November 2026. Cinemas worldwide get it on 5 May 2028. ## You Can See Everything crosses $100 million worldwide The documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, You Can See Everything, has crossed $100 million worldwide this week. TechCrunch reports, citing Variety figures, that the total has reached $102.4 million, with $93.4 million from the US and $9 million overseas. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim directed the film. ... ## Salman Khan confirms Dabangg 4 and rules out a Bajrangi Bhaijaan sequel Dabangg 4 will happen, Salman Khan has confirmed, saying a Dabangg sequel is in his family’s hands. The Times of India reports he was speaking at an ABP summit, where he also ruled out a Bajrangi Bhaijaan sequel, saying no follow-up could match the original emotionally. No release date or director has been announced.
